title: DC-area forecast: Scattered showers and storms today, very humid
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: Scattered showers and storms, maybe a few flooding downpours, continue into the afternoon, especially from near I-66, DC, and Route 50 to the north. There should be fewer showers and storms around, and mainly north of DC, after 2 p.m. or so.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Humidity is in full force today with highs in the 80s. Scattered showers and storms, maybe a few flooding downpours, continue into the afternoon, especially from near I-66, DC, and Route 50 to the north. There should be fewer showers and storms around, and mainly north of DC, after 2 p.m. or so.

What’s next? Staying humid and turning hotter tomorrow through the weekend. Shower and storm chances continue, mainly during the afternoons into evenings.

Today’s daily digit — 4/10: The heat holds back, but humidity makes a comeback, and we're dodging some showers and storms with a flood risk. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Wednesday): Mostly cloudy and very humid. Scattered showers and storms are possible into the afternoon, especially from near I-66, DC, and Route 50 to the north. Shower coverage may be rather spotty in many areas, and by mid- to late afternoon there may just be a few showers and a storm around, mainly north of DC. Highs are in the 80s with icky dew points in the low to mid-70s. A light breeze develops from the south this afternoon at about 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Tonight: A few scattered showers and a downpour are possible during the evening with lower rain chances overnight. Otherwise partly to mostly cloudy and staying super muggy with lows in the low to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Thursday): Partly sunny and hotter with highs heading for around 90 to 95. Continued high humidity (dew points still in low to mid-70s) helps the heat index peak in the upper 90s to near 100. The chance of isolated to scattered showers and storms is mainly during the late afternoon into evening and especially from near DC and I-95 to the west. With the higher heat, some storms could be strong to severe with localized flooding and damaging winds. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Isolated to scattered showers and storms, a few with potential to be strong to severe, remain possible during the evening. Partly cloudy and muggy overnight with lower rain chances and lows in the 70s. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

The weather pattern is pretty much stuck Friday through Sunday. Highs should be in the upper 80s to mid-90s, and it's still quite humid with dew points mainly in the low 70s. Late-day isolated to scattered showers and storms are possible each day, although chances may be lower on Sunday. Muggy nighttime lows are around 70 to 75. Confidence: Low-Medium

Similar heat and humidity look to stick around Monday and Tuesday. A chance for showers and storms may linger as well, with Tuesday perhaps having the higher chance.

DC weather history for August 5

Blistering heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 102 degrees amid a devastating drought, part of a summer that saw a record number of 100-degree days and severe agricultural losses.
